Splash.Scopes.Accounting.AddressProvider.technical:
This scope is a contract: the server commits to provide the shipping
address of its documents (orders, invoices, quotations and supplier
orders), in read mode. This is THE address an OMS or a WMS ships to.
- The address is written inline on the document with the generic postal
address fields (schema.org PostalAddress, Organization and Person tags),
the ones a WMS exposes on its orders. It is not a link to an Address
object, and not the [DA] delivery address family, which is used when a
document carries both its billing and delivery addresses inline.
- A document MUST send who the parcel is shipped to: the company name, OR
the full name, OR at least the last name. Sending firstname and lastname
separately is an improvement.
- A document MUST send the postal address: street, postal code, city and
ISO country code. The compliance test fails when one is missing, it is
never skipped: a sales site declaring this scope commits to give a
complete shipping address on every order.
- Street extension, email, phones, region code and the relay point are
improvements: they help the carrier, they are sent when known. The relay
point code travels in the address description field: when it is set,
the postal address is the one of the pickup point.
- The contract applies to every document type carrying a shipment. It is
a building block, meant to be aggregated in server features rather than
declared alone.

Splash.Scopes.Accounting.ItemsProvider.technical:
This scope is a contract: the server commits to provide its accounting
documents (orders, invoices, quotations, supplier orders and supplier
invoices) together with their lines, i.e. the detail of the products.
- Every line identifies its product by its Product link OR by its SKU: at
least one of the two fields is sent. Sending both is recommended.
- Every line carries the quantity and the unit price. The unit price is a
Splash price: amount without tax, tax rate, currency.
- Line description, discount, tax code, product name and line type
(product, shipping, discount...) are improvements: when the server has
them, it sends them, and the other applications get a faithful copy of
the document.
- The contract applies to every accounting document type the server
exposes. It is a building block, meant to be aggregated in server
features rather than declared alone.

Splash.Scopes.Accounting.ItemsReceiver.technical:
This scope is a contract: the server commits to receive the lines of its
accounting documents (orders, invoices, quotations, supplier orders and
supplier invoices) in write mode, and provides them back as an
Accounting Items Provider.
- The line product MUST be writable, by its Product link OR by its SKU: at
least one of the two fields is writable. A server that resolves its
products by SKU does not need to expose the Product link.
- The line quantity and unit price MUST be writable: the compliance test
fails otherwise, it is never skipped.
- The received list is the COMPLETE set of lines of the document: lines
missing from it are removed.
- Line description, discount, tax code and type are improvements in write
mode: when the server accepts them, the received document is a faithful
copy of the original one.
- The contract applies to every accounting document type the server
exposes. It is a building block, meant to be aggregated in server
features rather than declared alone.

Splash.Scopes.Accounting.MultiTrackingPr.technical:
This scope is a contract: the server commits to provide the tracking of
EVERY parcel of its shipments, in read mode, on top of the main parcel
tracking of the Tracking Provider scope.
- The parcels are sent as a list, one row per parcel, holding the parcel
tracking number and optionally its tracking url, shipping method code,
carrier name and delivery status.
- The list fields are the Shipments templates (schema.org
ParcelDeliveryCollection tags), distinct from the single Tracking fields
of the main parcel. A server exposing this scope exposes both, and the
main parcel appears in the list as well.
- The parcel tracking number MUST be sent for every row: the compliance
test fails otherwise, it is never skipped.
- The parcel tracking url is optional. The shipping method code, the
carrier name and the delivery status are improvements: the status is a
free value, as the shipping application names it.
- The contract applies to every document type carrying a shipment
(orders, invoices, quotations and supplier orders). It is a building
block, meant to be aggregated in server features rather than declared
alone.

Splash.Scopes.Accounting.PartiesProvider.technical:
This scope is a contract: the server commits to provide the parties of
its accounting documents (orders, invoices, quotations, supplier orders
and supplier invoices), i.e. the records the document is attached to.

the customer of a sales document, the supplier of a purchase document.
This field is mandatory, a document always belongs to a third party.
- The billing and shipping addresses as links to Address objects are
optional: a server that only holds the addresses inline (see the Billing
and Delivery scopes) does not expose these links. When exposed, they are
readable.
- Sending the currency of the document is an improvement: it is the
currency of every amount of the document.
- The contract applies to every accounting document type the server
exposes. It is a building block, meant to be aggregated in server
features rather than declared alone.

Splash.Scopes.Accounting.PartiesReceiver.technical:
This scope is a contract: the server commits to receive the parties of

and supplier invoices) in write mode, and provides them back as an

Splash.Scopes.Accounting.PaymentsProvide.technical:
This scope is a contract: the server commits to provide the payments of
its documents (orders, invoices and supplier invoices), in read mode, as
a list with one row per payment.
- Every payment MUST send its date and its amount: the compliance test
fails otherwise, it is never skipped. The amount is expressed in the
currency of the document.
- The payment transaction id is an improvement, but a STRONGLY
recommended one: bank transaction id, check number, payment gateway
reference... It is what lets a receiver recognise a payment it already
recorded, and never books it twice.
- The payment method is an improvement. It is a CODE, never a label,
preferably one of the Splash normalized codes of the PaymentMethods
dictionary (ByBankTransferInAdvance, CheckInAdvance, Cash, CreditCard,
PayPal...). The list is not exhaustive: a server may send its own codes
for methods the dictionary does not cover.

Splash.Scopes.Accounting.PaymentsReceive.technical:
This scope is a contract: the server commits to receive the payments of
its documents (orders, invoices and supplier invoices) in write mode, as

Payments Provider.
- Every payment MUST be writable with its date and its amount: the
compliance test fails otherwise, it is never skipped. The received list

recognise: a payment is never rejected because of its method. Codes are
preferably the Splash normalized codes of the PaymentMethods dictionary,
the list being not exhaustive.
- Receiving payments usually updates the paid status of the document:
this is the server decision, not part of this contract.
- The contract applies to every document type carrying payments. It is a
building block, meant to be aggregated in server features rather than
declared alone.

Splash.Scopes.Accounting.TotalsProvider.technical:
This scope is a contract: the server commits to provide the totals of its
accounting documents (orders, invoices, quotations, supplier orders and
supplier invoices), in read mode only. Totals are computed by the server
that owns the document, they are never written by Splash.
- Three totals are sent: products total, shipping total and discount
total. Each one is a Splash price: amount without tax, tax amount,
currency.
- ALL THREE fields are mandatory: the compliance test fails when one is
missing. A server that does not manage one of these amounts (no shipping
fees on quotations, no discounts...) still exposes the field and sends a
ZERO price, never an empty value. Readers rely on the three totals being
present to compute the amount of a document: products + shipping - discount.
- The grand total is optional: when the server has it, it sends the amount
of the document as it displays it, and readers use it instead of
computing it.
- The contract applies to every accounting document type the server
exposes. It is a building block, meant to be aggregated in server
features rather than declared alone.

Splash.Scopes.Accounting.TrackingClient.technical:
This scope is a contract in both directions between a shop and its
logistics: the server chooses the shipping method of its shipments, and
receives the tracking of its parcels in write mode. This is the shop
side: the application that took the order tells the OMS / WMS which
carrier to use, and gets the tracking back.
- The tracking number MUST be writable, and readable once received: the
compliance test fails otherwise, it is never skipped.
- The tracking url is optional: when exposed, it is writable.
- Both fields are those of the MAIN parcel: when a shipment has several
parcels, the shop receives the tracking of the first / main one here,
and the full list of parcels through a Multi Tracking Provider.
- Sending the shipping method code, and its human readable name, is an
improvement: the OMS / WMS then ships with the carrier and service the
customer chose.
- Receiving a tracking number usually moves the document to its shipped
status: this is the server decision, not part of this contract.
- The contract applies to every document type carrying a shipment
(orders, invoices, quotations and supplier orders). It is a building
block, meant to be aggregated in server features rather than declared
alone.

Splash.Scopes.Order.HybridStatusProvider.technical:
This scope is a contract in both directions between a shop and its OMS,
seen from the shop side: the shop decides whether an order is validated
or canceled, the OMS drives the order status from there.
The workflow, seen from both sides:
1. An order is created on the shop: it is a draft, its validated and
canceled flags are false. On the shop the order ALWAYS has a status, it
is never empty. The OMS receives the order but, as long as it is neither
validated nor canceled, it sends back an EMPTY status: the order keeps
living between the other systems, the OMS never overrides its status.
2. The shop validates the order: validated becomes true. From now on the
OMS drives the status: it sends the Splash order statuses (processing,
processed, in transit, delivered...) and the shop takes them.
3. Or the shop cancels the order: canceled becomes true. The order is
canceled on the OMS, which never sends a status for it afterwards.
4. Optionally, the shop raises the force delivered flag: it tells the OMS
that it handled the shipment elsewhere, and that the OMS only has to
take the items out of stock, without shipping. This feature is optional,
not every OMS can honour it.
Constraints on the shop:
- The validated and canceled flags MUST be readable: the compliance test
fails otherwise, it is never skipped. They are the shop decisions.
- The order status MUST be writable, and readable: it is set by the OMS
with the Splash normalized statuses once the order is validated. It is
never empty on the shop, and the shop never overrides a status set by
the OMS.
- The force delivered flag is optional: when exposed, it is readable.
The contract applies to orders only. It is a building block, meant to be
aggregated in server features rather than declared alone.

Splash.Scopes.Order.HybridStatusReceiver.technical:
This scope is a contract in both directions between a shop and its OMS,
seen from the OMS side: the OMS receives the shop decisions, validation
or cancellation, and drives the order status from there.
The workflow, seen from both sides:
1. An order is created on the shop: it is a draft, its validated and
canceled flags are false. On the shop the order ALWAYS has a status, it
is never empty. The OMS receives the order but, as long as it is neither
validated nor canceled, it sends back an EMPTY status: the order keeps
living between the other systems, the OMS never overrides its status.
2. The shop validates the order: validated becomes true. From now on the
OMS drives the status: it sends the Splash order statuses (processing,
processed, in transit, delivered...) and the shop takes them.
3. Or the shop cancels the order: canceled becomes true. The order is
canceled on the OMS, which never sends a status for it afterwards.
4. Optionally, the shop raises the force delivered flag: it tells the OMS
that it handled the shipment elsewhere, and that the OMS only has to
take the items out of stock, without shipping. This feature is optional,
not every OMS can honour it.
Constraints on the OMS:
- The validated and canceled flags MUST be writable: the compliance test
fails otherwise, it is never skipped. They are received from the shop.
- The order status MUST be readable: it is the OMS own progress, sent
to the shop with the Splash normalized statuses once the order is
validated. Before validation and after a cancellation the OMS returns an
EMPTY status, so that the shop status is never overridden.
- The force delivered flag is optional: an OMS able to take the items
out of stock without shipping exposes it in write mode, the others do
not expose it.
The contract applies to orders only. It is a building block, meant to be
aggregated in server features rather than declared alone.

Splash.Scopes.Order.InvoicingProvider.technical:

Splash.Scopes.Order.Oms.technical:
This server feature is the contract of an OMS or a WMS: the application

parcel. Multi-parcel tracking is a separate, optional feature.

cancellations, and drives the status of the orders it processes.

the accounting application, PDF first, and shows it to its customer.
A server declaring this feature commits to every constraint of these
base scopes.

Splash.Scopes.Product.BomProvider.technical:
This scope is a contract: the server commits to provide Product objects
together with their manufacturing bill of materials (BOM).
- A bill of materials describes how a product is manufactured: its
components are consumed by the production, through manufacturing orders,
and the manufactured product gets its own stock. Products sold together
without manufacturing are described by the kit scopes (Product.KitProvider).
- It sends, for every manufactured product, the list of its components:
each row links a component Product and gives the quantity consumed to
produce one unit of the product.
- Components are identified by their Product link OR by their SKU: at
least one of the two fields is sent. Sending both is recommended, the SKU
makes the bill of materials readable without resolving the links.
- A product without components sends an empty list. The optional "has BOM"
flag tells whether a product is manufactured without reading the list.
- Manufacturing data (costs, operations, lead times...) will extend this
subject with dedicated templates: this scope only covers the components.
- Typical use case: an ERP or a MRP sends the products catalog with their
bills of materials, a WMS or a manufacturing application collects them to
plan the production or compute the components consumption.

Splash.Scopes.Product.BomReceiver.technical:
This scope is a contract: the server commits to receive Product
manufacturing bills of materials (BOM) in write mode.
- A bill of materials describes how a product is manufactured: its
components are consumed by the production. Products sold together without

- The BOM component & quantity fields MUST be writable: the compliance test
fails otherwise, it is never skipped.
- The received list is the COMPLETE bill of materials of the product:
components missing from it are removed, an empty list removes the BOM.
- Components are identified by their Product link OR by their SKU: at
least one of the two fields MUST be writable. A server that resolves its
components by SKU does not need to expose the Product link.
- When the Product link is writable, the component SKU MAY be read-only,
as an information. The "has BOM" flag is optional and MAY be read-only:
the server deduces it from the list.
- Typical use case: a WMS or a manufacturing application receives, and
only receives, the bills of materials sent by an ERP or a MRP.

This scope is a contract: the server commits to provide Product objects

collects them from this server, which acts as the images source of truth.

legends are global to the gallery, while cover & visible flags are given
for the read variant only. On a variable product, each variant flags its
own visible images & cover: e.g. a red t-shirt variant shows the common
studio shot plus the red packshots, and hides the other colors packshots.
- Typical use case: a PIM sends the products catalog with the detail of
all their photos, other systems collect them.

Splash.Scopes.Product.GalleryReceiver.technical:

flags apply to the written variant only. On a variable product, each
variant flags its own visible images & cover: e.g. a red t-shirt variant
shows the common studio shot plus the red packshots, and hides the other

Splash.Scopes.Product.KitProvider.technical:
This scope is a contract: the server commits to provide Product objects
together with the composition of their kits.
- A kit is a set of existing products sold together as one item and
assembled when the order is prepared: it is not manufactured, each
component keeps its own stock and its own price. Manufactured products
are described by the bill of materials scopes (Product.BomProvider).
- It sends, for every kit, bundle or pack, the list of its components:
each row links a component Product and gives the quantity included in
one unit of the kit.
- Components are identified by their Product link OR by their SKU: at
least one of the two fields is sent. Sending both is recommended, the SKU
makes the kit readable without resolving the links.
- A product without components sends an empty list. The optional "is kit"
flag tells whether a product is a kit without reading the list.
- Any application that needs to know what a kit contains collects it
from this server, which acts as the kits source of truth.
- Typical use case: an ERP or a PIM sends the products catalog with the
composition of its kits, a WMS or an e-commerce platform collects them to
prepare orders or compute virtual stocks.

Splash.Scopes.SupplierOrder.Erp.technical:
This server feature is the contract of an ERP on the purchase side: the
application that PLACES the supplier orders and follows their delivery.
It aggregates, on supplier orders:
- Purchase Header as a provider: the supplier order goes out with its
number, its date and the expected arrival date of the goods.
- Supplier Items, Supplier, Shipping Address and Totals as a provider:
the supplier order goes out complete, with its lines, supplier
references, the code and name of its supplier, delivery address and
amounts. The supplier link comes on top when suppliers are synchronized,
it is never required.
- Receptions Receiver: the ERP receives, product by product, the
quantities delivered as told by the warehouse.
A server declaring this feature commits to every constraint of these
base scopes.

Splash.Scopes.SupplierOrder.ReceptionsPr.technical:
This scope is a contract: the server commits to provide the goods
receptions of its supplier orders, in read mode. This is the warehouse
side: the application that receives the goods tells what was delivered
against what was ordered, and an ERP declaring the Supplier Order Receptions
Receiver scope gets it.
- Receptions are sent as a list, parallel to the order lines, with one
row per product to receive.
- Every row identifies its product by its SKU, which MUST be sent: the
receptions are synchronized on the SKU. Sending the Product link and the
supplier reference (MPN) as well are improvements.
- Every row MUST send the ordered quantity and the received quantity:
the compliance test fails otherwise, it is never skipped. Comparing the
two tells whether the reception is complete, partial or pending. A
product not received yet sends a received quantity of ZERO, never an
empty value.
- The contract applies to supplier orders only. It is a building block,
meant to be aggregated in server features rather than declared alone.

Splash.Scopes.SupplierOrder.ReceptionsRe.technical:
This scope is a contract: the server commits to receive the goods
receptions of its supplier orders in write mode, and provides them back
as a Supplier Order Receptions Provider. This is the ERP side: the
application that placed the supplier order gets, from the warehouse,
what was actually delivered.
- Receptions are received as a list, parallel to the order lines, with
one row per product to receive. Rows are matched on the product SKU:
the SKU MUST be writable, it is the key of the synchronization. The
compliance test fails otherwise, it is never skipped.
- The received quantity MUST be writable: it is what the warehouse
sends. The ordered quantity is the server own data, exposed in read mode.
- Accepting the Product link and the supplier reference (MPN) on every
row are improvements.
- Receiving quantities usually updates the reception status of the
supplier order: this is the server decision, not part of this contract.
- The contract applies to supplier orders only. It is a building block,
meant to be aggregated in server features rather than declared alone.

Splash.Scopes.SupplierOrder.Wms.technical:
This server feature is the contract of a WMS, the warehouse: the
application that WAITS for the goods ordered to suppliers by an ERP,
receives them, and tells what was delivered. Unlike an OMS, it does not
process orders: it holds the stock the supplier orders feed.
It aggregates, on supplier orders:
- Purchase Header as a receiver: the supplier order arrives under the
ERP number, with its date and the expected arrival date the receptions
are planned on.
- Supplier Items, Supplier and Shipping Address as a receiver: the
supplier order arrives with its lines, supplier references, its supplier
and where the goods are delivered. The supplier is recognized by its
code or its name: the WMS does not need synchronized suppliers.
- Receptions Provider: the warehouse tells, product by product, what was
received against what was ordered.
A server declaring this feature commits to every constraint of these
base scopes.
